title: Contrix Service Describe
description: Canonical service describe response returned by cx.server.describe and per-surface describe operations. It combines stable service metadata (service_did, service_type, protocol_version, profiles, bindings, auth, limits, plaintext visibility and rate-limit policy) with claim-level partitions: implemented_features, claimed_profiles, verified_profiles, experimental_features and compat_surfaces. The legacy field `supported_operations` MUST list endpoint-callable operation_ids. Constraint: when `development_mode=true`, the service MUST NOT advertise any `verified_profiles` entry, and clients MUST verify cotest artifacts before treating verified_profiles as production conformance. See service-surface.md §3.0.

service_did.description: DID of the service endpoint making this describe claim.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_type.description: Registered lowercase service_type such as principal_server, sync_node, directory_service, push_gateway or applet_service.

supported_operations.description: operation_ids that this endpoint can actually be invoked with. Element format SHOULD match the canonical operation_registry ids (e.g. `cx.events.submit`).

supported_bindings.description: Transport binding declarations for this service.

supported_features.description: Feature identifiers (`cx.feature.*`) the service supports. Distinct from profile claims.

auth_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible.

implemented_features.description: feature_ids the service has implementation code for but does NOT necessarily claim conformance for. Tooling that builds a conformance matrix MUST treat this strictly weaker than `claimed_profiles`.

claimed_profiles.description: Profiles the service self-claims membership in. `claim_kind` MUST be `self_claimed`; verified-only assertions belong under `verified_profiles` and MUST NOT appear here.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a cotest run has produced a passing artifact. Each entry MUST identify the cotest run, the artifact hash, and the verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty.

experimental_features.description: feature_ids that the service exposes but explicitly does NOT promise stable interop for. Clients MUST treat these as non-load-bearing for protocol-level decisions.

compat_surfaces.description: Legacy or external-interop surfaces this service exposes for compatibility, not as part of its claimed Contrix v1 conformance.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.
